summary: Edge multipath preflight split causes model pin isolation loss during canary handoff
description: Issue summary: During a weighted canary promote for rw-gpt-3.2-compat, we observed tenant sessions losing their model pin and being routed to the fallback/degraded variant. This appears correlated with edge multipath preflight probes that create two concurrent handshake flows to the orchestrator.
detailed_description: Impact: Several BrightWave customers reported mixed model outputs and a spike in 5xx routing to degraded variant for a subset (~4%) of requests. Customer observed increased latency and model-output inconsistency during the 10:45–11:20 UTC canary window. Environment: Production, us-east1, Dedicated pool for BrightWave Analytics. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a gradual canary promote with weight 10% on rw-gpt-3.2-compat. 2) Enable multipath/connection-reuse at edge (simulate flaky TCP path multiplexing). 3) Replay tenant traffic with streaming sessions and interleaved keepalives. 4) Observe pin commit races where a preflight handshake on Path A commits a canary pin but Path B carries a stale control-plane snapshot that overwrites/evicts the pin. Observed behavior: - Mixed routing where subsequent requests from the same session hit legacy/degraded variant. - Edge logs show two preflight handshakes within 200ms for the same session token. - Orchestrator logs show conflicting commit order: "commit_pin tenant=brightwave session=abc123 variant=canary seq=402" then later "commit_pin tenant=brightwave session=abc123 variant=legacy seq=399" (seq numbers indicate stale snapshot on second flow). Expected behavior: Preflight handshakes should establish deterministic pin commit ordering; stale snapshots should not overwrite a later commit for the same session. Initial hypothesis: Edge multipath causes duplicate preflight handshakes to reach different orchestrator replicas with diverging epoch/snapshot states. Orchestrator currently accepts commit if snapshot_seq >= last_seen_seq per replica, but there is a window where a stale replica's write can arrive after a newer commit from another replica and be accepted, producing pin rollback. Temporary mitigation applied: - Support throttled BrightWave traffic to 5% of peak to reduce multipath pressure. - Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy to clamp preflight retries for known keepalive reconnect patterns. Investigation notes: - Snapshot sync lag between orchestrator replicas observed on tracing spans (max lag ~350ms under load). - Prewarm agent sometimes forwards preflight probes directly to worker nodes bypassing orchestration caching layer, increasing exposure to stale state. - No model quantization or serving changes during window. Next steps: 1) SRE to patch orchestrator commit acceptance to use monotonic commit tokens (in-flight patch PR referenced). 2) Engineering to add idempotent commit guard at edge-proxy for preflight flows. 3) Plan a controlled canary replay with multipath enabled in staging to validate fix. 4) Postmortem to be prepared and shared with BrightWave.

impact_summary: ~4% of BrightWave traffic experienced transient routing to legacy/degraded variant during canary window; increased latency and mismatch in outputs reported by customer; potential billing discrepancy flagged due to unexpected variant execution.
workarounds: Clamped preflight retries at edge and temporarily reduced traffic weight for BrightWave canary cohort. Advised customer to retry affected sessions; prepared manual pin re-assertion tool for urgent rebinds.
